name: sar-logic-timing-gates
description: Gate-level replay of sim/sar-logic-timing/ (issue #11's synchronous-SAR timing-margin/tie-handling verification, DR-0008) against the SYNTHESIZED gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v, issue #272) instead of the ideal rung-1 XSPICE sar_ctrl_a model, over the block's ratified PVT corner grid (issue #273, DR-0023 follow-on (a) continuation).
claim: README.md#target-specification -- Latency/conversion-timing row and the per-cycle timing budget in spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2, re-checked on the real synthesized gate netlist instead of the ideal rung-1 model. Substantiates the same sync-vs-async row of spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3 the rung-1 sibling does, now on real gf180mcu standard cells.
netlist_provenance: schematic (gate-level: klt-synthesized gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist wrapping sar_ctrl.v, issue #272 -- not yet placed-and-routed; DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c) own P&R/STA)

abs_err_delay_0ns.description: Reference -- UNCHANGED bound from the rung-1 ideal sibling (sim/sar-logic-timing/testbench/tb.json). With no added decision delay, every conversion in the run must still be exact on the real gate netlist.

abs_err_delay_40ns.description: THE SLACK CLAIM, spent in one place -- unchanged bound. Re-checks that the ~40 ns margin spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2 budgets is really available, now with real gf180mcu logic (not ideal XSPICE primitives) implementing the sequencer that has to consume its own share of that margin between the comparator decision and the next latching edge.

abs_err_delay_50ns.description: 80% of the bit cycle consumed -- unchanged bound. NOT RE-BISECTED here: this replay re-checks the SAME bisected boundary the rung-1 ideal sibling measured (0/40/50/70 ns bracket), it does not re-derive a new boundary for the gate-level netlist -- re-bisecting against a different DUT is a distinct claim, out of scope for this record (a candidate follow-on if the gate-level margin turns out tighter than the ideal one).

abs_err_delay_70ns.description: NEGATIVE CONTROL -- unchanged bound. 70 ns exceeds the 62.5 ns bit cycle; the conversion MUST come out wrong, on the real gate netlist exactly as on the ideal one.

tie_code_deviation.description: EXACT-TIE HANDLING -- unchanged bound. The code must land on one of the two adjacent codes (511 or 512) even on a real comparator-decision race, implemented by the same behavioural comparator model driving real gf180mcu sequencer logic.

tie_conv_period_ns.description: THE CADENCE CLAIM UNDER THE TIE -- unchanged bound. Even with the comparator deciding a dead tie every conversion, drdy must keep arriving exactly 16 clocks apart, now measured on real gf180mcu logic rather than ideal XSPICE digital primitives -- this is the concrete, gate-level form of the sync-vs-async row (spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.3).

ok_conv_period_ns.description: same cadence on the undisturbed loop -- unchanged bound.

acq_window_ns.description: DR-0014 ACQUISITION WINDOW -- bound REVISED by DR-0028 (spec/decision-records/DR-0028-gate-level-acquisition-isolation-bounds.md, issue #319) from the inherited 187.3..188.0 ns. That pair was set by rounding the rung-1 ideal deck's SINGLE tt/27C measurement (187.625 ns, sim/sar-logic-timing/records/20260802-102758-d8a363d.md) taken on an XSPICE model with fixed T_CLK_Q/T_GATE placeholders and no process axis at all, then copied unchanged into this manifest; it appears in no spec file and no decision record. THE LIMITS HERE ARE DERIVED FROM THE MARGIN, NOT FROM A MEASUREMENT. LOWER LIMIT 175.0 ns = the settling floor: DR-0013's input-pin redistribution kick is 1024*C_in/(C_in+C_pin) = 83.06 LSB at the worst permitted C_pin = 100 pF, recovered with tau_in <= 30 ns (DR-0013's contract ceiling), so allocating 0.25 LSB -- half the 1/2-LSB settling criterion, to keep the term negligible rather than merely legal -- to the un-recovered residual at the sampling instant requires 30*ln(83.06/0.25) = 174.17 ns, rounded UP so the limit is never looser than its derivation. (NOT DR-0001's t/tau >= ln(2^11) = 7.62 full-scale-step rule, which would demand 228.6 ns: DR-0013 supersedes DR-0001 precisely by replacing the full-scale-step model with the pinned-capacitor one, in which the pin never takes a full-scale step.) UPPER LIMIT 218.7 ns = DR-0003's 4-clock sample phase (4 x 62.5 = 250 ns) less iso_gap_ns's 31.25 ns ordering floor, rounded DOWN. acq_window_ns + iso_gap_ns is measured at 250.09..250.50 ns at all 45 PVT points of the per-loop `ok` deck's grid (sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/records/20260918-233547-1d81aa1.md -- this five-loop deck has never produced a scored point), i.e. the sel_in_n pulse IS that 250 ns phase everywhere, so these two measurements are ONE degree of freedom and each upper limit is the other measurement's floor restated. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT: every input (DR-0013's tau_in/C_pin contract, DR-0003's 62.5 ns phase, the 1/2-LSB criterion) is a spec quantity P&R does not change, so this is one limit pre- AND post-layout, not a pre-layout number to be re-baselined. Worst slack measured to date, PRE-LAYOUT: 1.93 ns at fs_125c_2.97v (176.927 ns) -- thin, and deliberately so: P&R/extraction (#274/#275) is a real test of this floor, and breaking it there would be a genuine design-closure finding, not another widening.

iso_gap_ns.description: DR-0014's TWO-PHASE SAMPLE: the isolation gap, and its SIGN is the ordering claim -- bound REVISED by DR-0028 (issue #319) from the inherited 62.2..62.8 ns, which has the same idealised single-corner origin as acq_window_ns above. LOWER LIMIT 31.3 ns = the ordering floor, half of one DR-0003 clock phase (31.25 ns, rounded UP). POSITIVE means sel_in_n falls LAST -- the input legs turn off onto an already-isolated node, which is the entire mechanism of DR-0014 -- and both real failure modes are a whole clock phase in size (second phase DROPPED -> 0 ns; the two phases SWAPPED -> -62.5 ns), so a half-phase floor still fails decisively on both, by 31.25 ns and 93.75 ns. It leaves 22.0 ns beyond the worst PVT excursion measured (53.3104 ns at sf_125c_2.97v, 9.19 ns below the 62.5 ns nominal) -- 2.4x that excursion -- as headroom for P&R interconnect skew, extracted parasitics and on-die mismatch, none of which this pre-layout netlist has. UPPER LIMIT 75.0 ns = the 250 ns sample phase less acq_window_ns's 175.0 ns settling floor: excess isolation is missing acquisition, and by the sum invariant noted above this ceiling IS that floor restated. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT, for the same reason as acq_window_ns. Worst slack to date, PRE-LAYOUT: 22.0 ns on the floor, 1.67 ns on the ceiling (73.3269 ns at fs_125c_2.97v). The asymmetry is the finding: input settling is the binding constraint on the two-phase sample, and the ordering claim itself is robust across the whole PVT box.

notes: PVT GRID: unlike the rung-1 ideal sibling (no PDK device models, so process/temperature cannot move anything and only tt/27C is run), this deck wraps a real synthesized gf180mcu netlist and is therefore swept over the full ratified mos corner-set (tt/ff/ss/fs/sf) x -40/27/125 C x +/-10% supply -- 45 points -- exactly the grid #273 was filed to run. A given run's actual record states which corner points it covers (see 'Subset-corner justification' in sim/README.md) if fewer than the full 45 were run -- see this experiment's own records/ for what was actually executed and why.

COMPUTATIONAL COST, MEASURED: this deck's five loops (ok/lt/xl/bad/tie) share ONE clock, so their combined circuit sees near-continuous switching activity across the whole 8.5 us run rather than each loop's own quieter, well-separated edges -- measured, while building this record, at up to two orders of magnitude slower per simulated nanosecond than a single loop run in isolation (a single loop's own 8.5 us run took ~55 s; the full five-loop deck took over one hundred times as long per ns of simulated time during its densest early interval). This is the reason a given run of the full 45-point mos grid on this deck is a substantial undertaking (on the order of an hour or more per corner point) and why individual records may legitimately cover a stated subset -- see 'Subset-corner justification', sim/README.md.

The delay values (0/40/50/70 ns) are the SAME bisected bracket the rung-1 ideal sibling measured -- this record re-checks that bracket against the gate-level netlist, it does not re-bisect a new one (see abs_err_delay_50ns's own description).

SEEDING: design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note' applies -- every loop in this deck drives its own start net high for 2 whole clock periods from t=0 before dropping it (gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's START_PULSE_CLOCKS), establishing the ph ring's one-hot invariant before any other output is trusted. The rung-1 ideal sibling never needed this.

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model, the delay-insertion mechanism (an ideal lossless transmission line, ahead of the real gate logic) and the tie/negative-control loops are all UNCHANGED from the rung-1 sibling (same _loop()/_timing_body() composition in gen_sar_logic.py) -- only the DUT subckt sar_ctrl_a changed, from the ideal XSPICE model to the real synthesized netlist.

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour, unchanged from the rung-1 sibling's own disclosure.

ISSUE #282 (RESOLVED) -- see sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/'s tb.json for the full write-up: ngspice did not converge the translated gate-level sar_ctrl_a DUT to a valid digital operating point (confirmed on the DUT alone, no CDAC loop, and confirmed not to be a translation bug by isolated-instance reproduction). Root cause was a missing `.global vdd_gate` declaration -- the supply net every standard cell binds is supplied from OUTSIDE the emitted subckt, so without it SPICE scoped the net LOCALLY per instance, leaving the DUT unpowered. `design/sar-logic/flow/gate_netlist_to_spice.py` now emits that declaration (plus a structural guard), validated on a standalone non-closed-loop probe deck before landing here.

A CORNER-GRID RUN IS RECORDED HERE: this experiment has populated records/, corners/ and netlist-snapshots/ directories, and its first corner-grid run is sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/records/20260915-210638-912a8ec.md -- the full 45-point mos grid, executed under issue #289. Read that record for the per-point error signatures; this note does not summarise them beyond the one fact a reader must not miss: it records 0 of 45 points converged, not a passing grid. That failure is a defect distinct from #282's (which only ever concerned the DC operating point); it was diagnosed and fixed separately under issue #296, and re-running the grid on top of that fix is tracked as issue #303. HISTORY (kept because it explains the gap between this deck being written and its first grid being recorded): before that run the deck carried no corner-grid run at all -- first because of #282's now-fixed non-convergence blocker, and then, after that fix, for a DIFFERENT reason: this deck's own COMPUTATIONAL COST note above (measured at up to two orders of magnitude slower per simulated ns than a single isolated loop, 'on the order of an hour or more per corner point') makes the full 45-point mos grid a substantial undertaking that #282's own session could not complete on top of severe, measured host contention that session hit while calibrating the sibling functional-gates deck (a single nominal-corner point there took over an hour of wall-clock time against an ~8.4-minute CPU estimate). That pure execution/recording follow-on was tracked as issue #289, which has since run the grid -- it never reopened the convergence question #282 answered.
